proof_checks: Finite-valued nearest-point approximants to a fixed dense Hilbert sequence prove strong measurability, including H={0}.
Bounded angular maps and probability second moments imply finite first weight moments, hence finite Bochner moment and penalty.
AC selects couplings with RMS displacement delta_n->0.
Pullback of simple approximants under marginal projections preserves their L1 errors and integral, so no unsupported Bochner change-of-variable theorem is assumed.
Moment difference <= (||phi||infinity+Lip(phi)*sqrt(integral |w|^2 dmu))*delta_n; the factor uses the fixed limit law.
Penalty difference obeys the same bound since ||w|-|wprime||<=|w-wprime|.
Continuity of R at the limiting moment proves convergence of risk; no differential, sublevel bound or derivative of phi is used.
Smooth-model finite branch has identical data and finite integrals, so the local-to-upstream F identity is literal.
